title: release.yml validates its window variables before publishing, and PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS uses a real grammar instead of parseInt
description: Found by the LCLI-630 implementer and reviewer (#358, 2026-09-28). LCLI-630 made the post-publish visibility wait refuse a malformed REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS, but the guard fires only AFTER npm publish, so a bad variable fails a release that did publish, and publish:false rehearsals never see it. The reviewer also found a fifth window reader outside the shared grammar: release.yml:1501 passes vars.PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS to release-provenance.mjs, which parses it with parseInt (~line 993): 30m->30, 08->8, 1e3->1, abc throws. Not injectable (quoted node argument). Measured at #358 head 2edab0a3 by the reviewer; no variable is set today (0 repo, 0 release-environment, 0 visible org variables). Also update docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md (~line 800, the LCLI-629 paragraph) to list release.yml as a reader of the window.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release.yml refuses a malformed vars.REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS and vars.PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS BEFORE the first npm publish (and in publish:false rehearsals), naming the variable and showing the value escaped, so a bad variable can no longer fail a release that already published

PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS is validated against the shared REGISTRY_WINDOW grammar (or a stated grammar of its own) instead of parseInt: 30m, 08, 1e3 and abc are refused, proven by tests; the pattern is pinned to its source
The post-publish guard LCLI-630 added stays (defence in depth) or its removal is argued on this task
bun test, lint:shell, actionlint and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the release.yml change
